item.title: Nasdaq slips as Nvidia sells off, but stocks post their best week since August
item.description: The Nasdaq fell 0.91% on Friday and the S&P 500 slid 0.4%, while the Dow edged up 0.1%. Even so, all three major averages notched their best weekly performance since early August. Investors rotated into other tech names such as Apple, AMD and Broadcom.

item.title: Nvidia names CFO Colette Kress interim CEO after Jensen Huang resigns
item.description: Nvidia said Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive and from the board, effective immediately. Chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor. Shares ended the week down about 13%.

item.title: Bessent says Commerce controls decision on blacklisting Nvidia customer Megaspeed
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said several agencies had backed adding Megaspeed to the entity list for months. He said the decision rests with the Commerce Department. Megaspeed denies diverting chips to China.

item.title: Anthropic IPO: AI company seeks valuation of more than $1 trillion
item.description: Anthropic set a price range of $70 to $78 a share for its initial public offering. The company is expected to price and begin trading next week on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. The deal will test investor sentiment toward artificial intelligence.

item.title: Modine shares soar on report Samsung is in talks to acquire the company
item.description: Shares of Modine Manufacturing jumped more than 25% after a report that Samsung Electronics is in talks to buy the maker of thermal management equipment. The companies could reach a deal in the coming weeks.
